blindSummary:
This state/province was the second-worst unit nationally in 2024 with 12 killings and tied for the top in 2025 with 8 (matching the regional leader). Against a population of ~21 million, the 2025 rate of ~0.38 per million matches the national per-million figure — but the consistency of appearing in the top two across both years signals a structurally elevated environment compared with states whose counts fluctuate. The 2024 total of 12 placed it behind only the most populous unit.

Compared with the much smaller state that matched its 2025 absolute count, this state/province's per-capita exposure is roughly half — a more moderate elevation; compared with the most populous state, which led the 2024 count (16) but fell sharply in 2025, the distinguishing risk factor here is that two-year consistency rather than a single-year spike.

No state-specific legal restriction or unique ordinance was identified. For a visitor the risk is violence exposure, patterned over two years, in a large inland unit where the dossier's finding that most killings occur outside capitals implies added danger away from the main metro.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional news portal write-up (27 Jan 2025) of the trans-movement association's 2024 dossier: 122 killings of trans and travesti people, 16% below 2023's 145 and under the 2008-2024 average; the worst units were the most populous state (16), this state/province (12) and the regional leader (11), with three remote northern units unrecorded; at least 68% of cases occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 95.9% of victims were travestis/trans women; Antra criticises chronic official under-notification.

National news report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th association dossier: 80 killings nationwide in 2025 (down 34%, still world's highest); this state/province ties for the top of the 2025 state ranking with 8, against the regional leader's 8 on a far smaller population; 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% outside capitals; 1,261 killings 2017-2025.
